pos.personaBrief: Chile and La U built from deep with Juego de Posicion and controlled games (El Gráfico, Spielverlagerung); he said they learned to defend with the ball.

pro.personaBrief: Short build-up from the keeper and centre-backs even under press, with fast vertical transitions after regaining the ball (Spielverlagerung, Bleacher Report); he admitted earlier being more direct.

est.personaBrief: Bielsista fluid structure with heavy rotation of midfielders, back-three players stepping out as full-backs, and 3-2-5 shapes; central overloads and short combinations.

lar.personaBrief: Chile stretched the pitch laterally with high wide full-backs and wing-backs, but also stressed central orientation through midfield overloads and no classic wingers.

blo.personaBrief: High line near halfway, immediate counterpress and pressing the man on the ball almost always (Ballverliebt, Spielverlagerung, Sportskeeda).

mar.personaBrief: Back line man-marked players dropping to receive, and Medel man-marked the lone striker vs Spain; Messi was tightly controlled in the final.

pla.personaBrief: Strong imposed identity with Bielsista model, but with notable per-game tweaks (five-man line vs Spain, 4-1-2-1-2 vs Bolivia) and more caution against powers.

res.personaBrief: Gung-ho 'eleven kamikazes' attacking football valued for style, kept attacking even against bigger sides; some pragmatism at Copa America 2015.

sis.personaBrief: Strongly systemic collective with rotations and pressing duties for all, though he tolerated Vidal and Valdivia roamed freely as the brain.

jog.personaBrief: Very high physical intensity pressing, yet technically capable players comfortable on the ball (Diaz, Bravo, Valdivia) were prized.

bas.personaBrief: Planned to select best juveniles at La U and debuted 15-year-olds, but won with a national team of established players like Vidal and Sanchez.

lid.personaBrief: Obsessive disciplinarian who suspended Aranguiz for oversleeping, yet turned a blind eye to Vidal and built a fanatical, devoted group.
